Introduction
The automatic CO2 gas fire extinguishing system consists of a number of cylinders containing carbon dioxide gas in its liquid state under a pressure of approximately 80 bar. The cylinders are arranged in groups according to the quantity of gas required for extinguishing, and each group is dedicated to extinguishing a fire in a specific area matching the volume of gas inside these cylinders. There are extinguishing gas nozzles and flame detectors distributed as shown in the following table:
Flame detector | Heat detector | Nozzles | Number of cylinders | 
1 | 4 | 4 | 3 | Right combustion chamber
1 | 4 | 4 | 3 | Left combustion chamber
1 | 4 | 8 | 7 | Oil tank
Each of the flame and heat detectors has two independent lines, and for the fire system to operate a fire alarm signal must come from one of the fire detectors on the first line together with an alarm from one of the fire detectors on the second line. The weight-release solenoid then moves, the fire system operates, and at the same time the emergency trip signal goes from the limit switch to the various components of the unit so that they stop.
The cylinder weighing device is the indicator of leakage of the extinguishing agent from the carbon dioxide cylinder. The leak indicator device is adjusted so that it gives a leakage signal when the cylinder loses extinguishing agent up to a maximum of 10% of the total weight of the cylinder, at which point cylindrical weight No. 1 drops down; this is the indication that the cylinder weight has fallen as a result of gas leakage, and the cylinder is then replaced.
This document was prepared by Eng. Yousry Abdel Halim Abdel Latif, tested by Eng. Wasfy William Nashed – Senior Engineer, Occupational Safety and Health Department – and approved by Eng. Soliman Zaki Soliman, General Manager of Quality Assurance and Quality Control, and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed Farag Anan – Head of Damietta Power Station Sector – and Eng. Mohamed Hussein Gomaa, Head of Quality Assurance and Quality Control Sector, East Delta Electricity Production Company.

Open a work order by the Occupational Safety and Health Department |

Procedure to be Carried Out
Release the cylindrical weight to undo the locking nuts No. 3 | 1.
Turn the cylindrical weight No. 1 anticlockwise on the threaded shaft No. 2 until the cylindrical weight is just horizontally balanced | 2.
Turn the cylindrical weight clockwise by three turns | 3
Tighten the locking nuts No. 3 and secure the position of the cylindrical weight with locking wire No. 4 | 4
